To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we developed techniques for measuring the energy spectra of protons and helium in circumterrestrial regions, and we obtained the energy spectra of cosmic rays in the energy range from 50 GeV to 1.5 TeV.
the energy spectrum of cosmic ray protons and helium in the energy range of 50-500 GeV is described well by a power-law function with a slope that does not change with the energy.

the measured spectra of protons and helium are in agreement with the spectra measured by other space experiments, and the spectra are consistent with the results of the direct measurements of the cosmic ray fluxes at the Earth’s surface.

we have developed a new method for measuring cosmic rays with energies of 100-1000 GeV.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the energy resolution of the calorimeter in the energy range 50 GeV-10 TeV is 10-20% for protons and 15-20% for helium nuclei.
the helium nuclei flux is about 2.4 times smaller than the proton flux.
